clue.text: Not a clear-cut issue for intelligence

definitions.meaning: a matter that is neither black nor white is in the grey area
the brain's grey tissue stands for brainpower or wits

explanation.surface: Someone muses that intelligence is a murky subject with no easy answers.
explanation.definitionFit: The first is a pun on a matter in a grey area; the second is the everyday term for brains or wits.

clue.text: Where circus performers go like the clappers?

definitions.meaning: the circular arena of a circus
what bells do when their clappers strike

explanation.surface: Circus acts rush in at great speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go like the clappers' is British slang for moving very fast; here clappers are the tongues of bells.
explanation.definitionFit: The circus arena is so called, and bells sound when clappers strike them.

clue.text: Arabian republic contains nothing but smallholders

indicators.note: the republic's name holds the other piece within it

parts.note: Yemen is a republic on the Arabian peninsula
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: An Arab country is said to hold only small farmers.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically, English freeholders farming their own modest land were called this.

clue.text: Eternal but unavailing plea Aurora doubtless made to Tith, onus

definitions.meaning: never ageing or ending

definitions.text: unavailing plea Aurora doubtless made to Tith, onus
definitions.meaning: in myth the dawn goddess won Tithonus immortality but forgot eternal youth; split, the word is a plea to grow old less

explanation.surface: A mythological goddess begs in vain for her mortal lover to stop growing old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tith, onus' is the printed split of Tithonus, the mortal lover of Aurora, who aged endlessly; the answer read as two words is the plea she should have made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something timeless never grows old; split in two, it is a request to age less.

clue.text: Lawrence the recipient of a book dedication? You can bet on it

definitions.text: Lawrence the recipient of a book dedication?
definitions.meaning: a book dedicated .... Lawrence would be inscribed to him with his initials
a betting system, the totalisator

explanation.surface: A dedication to Lawrence of Arabia is a sure thing.
explanation.walkthrough: The tote is the totalisator, the pool-betting system at British racecourses.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it is the inscription 'To T.E.'; whole, it is the racecourse betting system.

clue.text: Smoking jackets?

parts.note: read as cannabis cigarettes that are also a kind of short double-breasted coat

explanation.surface: A question about loungewear for the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both cannabis cigarettes, which are smoked, and short sailors' jackets.

clue.text: Go down to the Department of Employment with reformed teenager

parts.note: DE was the abbreviation for the UK Department of Employment

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A youth is sent to the employment office after turning over a new leaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformed' is the anagram signal on the teenager; 'Go down' is a verb meaning decline, not a direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To deteriorate or decline in quality is to go downhill.

clue.text: North African campaigners leave traitors behind

indicators.note: the traitors come after the first piece

parts.note: to desert is to abandon or leave
rats are informers or turncoats

explanation.surface: Wartime soldiers in Africa abandon the turncoats in their ranks.
explanation.walkthrough: The Desert Rats were the British 7th Armoured Division in the North African campaign of the Second World War.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname of British troops who fought in the North African desert in WWII.

clue.text: In attendance. Hear, hear!

indicators.note: the repeated word tells the solver to listen, so the first word counts only for its sound

parts.note: the word as spoken

explanation.surface: A roll call answered with a parliamentary cry of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear, hear!' looks like applause, but the second 'hear' asks you to listen to the first, which sounds like the word meaning present.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who is present at roll call answers that they are in this place.

clue.text: Nine tipsy imbibers have had it

definitions.meaning: nine is a single unit more than ..., read literally
the idiom for having drunk a little too much, said of tipsy drinkers

explanation.surface: Nine drunken revellers have reached the end of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: The British idiom means slightly drunk; read literally it is the number nine, one more than eight.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken literally the phrase is arithmetic for nine, and as idiom it describes a drinker who has had a glass too many.

clue.text: Rip off a wool-producer

definitions.meaning: to swindle or overcharge someone
a sheep's coat yields wool when shorn

explanation.surface: A con trick involving a sheep.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to swindle; as a noun it is the woolly coat shorn from a sheep.

clue.text: He's nice in a way, but foreign to us

indicators.note: in a different way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: its letters, the possessive apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone describes a pleasant but alien stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a way' signals rearranging HESNICE. The definition plays on the saying that something baffling 'is Chinese to me'.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of China is the proverbial example of something incomprehensible or foreign to an English speaker.

clue.text: Very simple drama staged in the junior school

definitions.meaning: an extremely easy task

definitions.text: drama staged in the junior school
definitions.meaning: a play performed by young children

explanation.surface: An easy little play put on by young pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A very easy task is idiomatically something a youngster could do; literally, a play by youngsters.

clue.text: I learnt not to be unorthodox or bigoted

indicators.note: unorthodox means irregular, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to give up unconventional ways or narrow-mindedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwilling to accept views or people different from one's own; prejudiced.

clue.text: See 10
Make the introduction now

definitions.meaning: to introduce one person formally to another
the current time, as opposed to past or future

explanation.surface: A host is told to do the introductions straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to introduce formally; as a noun or adjective it means the current moment.

clue.text: Write to a Liberal of punitive measures

parts.note: to pen is to write

explanation.surface: A letter is sent to a Liberal politician about punishments.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to punishment, as in a penal code or colony.

clue.text: Factions succeeded the day Caesar was murdered

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies
Julius Caesar was killed on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: Rival groups took over on the Ides of March after Caesar's assassination.
explanation.definitionFit: Opposing groups in a dispute are the parties or camps on each side.

clue.text: In Greece I find it symbolises very little

definitions.meaning: the Greek alphabet's letter corresponding to I
a tiny amount, as in 'not one jot'

explanation.surface: A traveller in Greece finds a symbol meaning almost nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet, and also idiomatically a minute quantity.

clue.text: Bye-bye, and thanks again

indicators.note: the word is said a second time, so its letters appear twice

parts.note: TA is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: A parting farewell with repeated thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A childish or informal British farewell, a synonym of goodbye.

clue.text: The woman has a right to make cuts

parts.note: a female person is referred to as she

explanation.surface: A woman asserts her entitlement to trim things.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut with large blades, as when clipping sheep or hedges.

clue.text: A kick in the leg at a noisy party

indicators.note: the kick lands on the leg, so the leg comes first

parts.note: the shin is the front of the lower leg
a dig is a poke or jab

explanation.surface: Someone gets kicked in the leg at a rowdy party.
explanation.definitionFit: A lively, noisy celebration or party.

clue.text: A little delicacy served on toast

definitions.meaning: a small piece that is uncommon, a choice bite
Welsh ... is a cheese dish served on toast

explanation.surface: A small treat is presented on toast.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is a British dish of melted cheese sauce on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Split, it is an uncommon bit; whole, it is cheese on toast.

clue.text: Two consecutive notes shed illumination, and that's a pleasure

parts.note: D and E are neighbouring notes of the musical scale
illumination is light

explanation.surface: A pair of musical notes give out light, which is enjoyable.
explanation.definitionFit: Great joy or gratification is a synonym for pleasure.

clue.text: Distribution of gifts in a well, attended Sunday School

parts.note: a well-attended gathering is a large one
SS is the abbreviation for Sunday School

explanation.surface: Presents are handed out at a well-attended Sunday School.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma in 'well, attended' is likely an OCR artefact for 'well-attended'.
explanation.definitionFit: Generous giving of money or presents is known as munificence or bounty.

clue.text: Root for a girl cooking head of celery

indicators.note: cooking means being worked up or concocted, so the letters are mixed
this word picks out the opening letter, or opening letters, of the words it governs

explanation.surface: Someone supports a girl preparing a celery dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooking' rearranges AGIRL into GARLI; 'head of' gives the C of celery.
explanation.definitionFit: The edible bulb of a plant in the onion family, used as a seasoning.

clue.text: The average fellow makes allowance

parts.note: par is the standard or average level
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: An ordinary man shows tolerance.
explanation.definitionFit: Excusing a fault is a form of indulgence, making allowance for it.

clue.text: A holiday paradise? I'll say!

indicators.note: say asks for the words to be spoken so the sound counts

parts.note: the contraction of I will, spoken

explanation.surface: Someone enthusiastically agrees that a place is a holiday paradise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll say!' looks like an exclamation of agreement, but 'say' asks you to hear I'll.
explanation.definitionFit: A small island is the stereotypical tropical holiday paradise.

clue.text: Printing instruction found in most Etruscan manuscripts

indicators.note: the letters are located within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: An editorial mark appears in most ancient Etruscan writings.
explanation.definitionFit: A proofreader's instruction meaning 'let it stand', cancelling a correction.

clue.text: Diana's competence proves to bea handicap

parts.note: DI is short for Diana, plus the S of the possessive
competence is ability

explanation.surface: Diana's skill turns out to be a hindrance.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'bea' is a typesetting slip for 'be a'.
explanation.definitionFit: An impairment that limits a person is a handicap.

clue.text: Bill gets born with a skin complaint

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
NE is from French né, born, used in giving maiden names

explanation.surface: A man named Bill is born with spotty skin.
explanation.definitionFit: An inflammatory condition of the skin producing spots and pimples.

clue.text: Good heavens! What a grand writer sir Walter was!

parts.note: grand means great
Sir Walter Scott was the Scottish novelist of Ivanhoe

explanation.surface: An exclamation of admiration for the novelist Sir Walter Scott.
explanation.definitionFit: An old-fashioned exclamation of surprise, like goodness me.
